shadows.name: sheet-drop

shadows.name: led-glow
shadows.purpose: Lit glyphs on the board only; lamps use 0 0 6-8px currentColor.

shadows.name: object-lift-presentation
shadows.purpose: A real product element placed on a pitch slide as a cut-out image (ticket, board); the shadow follows its alpha shape.

motion.name: ease-feed
motion.purpose: Every feed, drop and lamp-on in the world.

motion.name: paper-feed
motion.purpose: Ticket feeds down from the dispenser/printer.

motion.name: cell-drop
motion.value: 520ms; delay 300ms + 70ms per cell; opacity 0, translateY(-55%), blur(3px) -> rest
motion.purpose: Reference prints cell by cell on submit.

motion.name: led-check
motion.value: 1100ms; amber held 0-65%, then the row's own colour; delay 900ms + 160ms per row; the upload link's requirement board starts at 0ms
motion.purpose: Two-phase rule check: amber 'Check' then result.

motion.name: led-out / led-in
motion.value: 1100ms; checking word out at 85-100%, result word in at 70-100%
motion.purpose: Cross-fade of the board state word.

motion.name: change-lamp
motion.value: 1100ms; lamp + word hold amber 0-65%, then the new state's colour; only when the state changes while watched
motion.purpose: Console queue/slip lamps relight after an approval or a call ending.

motion.name: wait-in
motion.purpose: A loading screen appears only if the wait outlasts a blink; fast loads never flash a skeleton.

motion.name: wait-breathe
motion.purpose: Unprinted lines and unlit cells breathe while waiting. The world's only loop, on waiting shapes only.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Keys and links never nudge, lift or press in.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All motion collapses to its end state; the wait breathe stops and the skeleton simply appears, still.

components.name: Auto-Call Switch
components.description: Console bar toggle (aria-pressed): 8px lamp (steady green on, 25% unlit off) + 'Auto-call' + 13px Doto ON/OFF. Turning on asks inline like Reset demo: 12.5px hint at 80% LED text (≤46ch at lg, own row below lg, aria-describedby), Cancel takes focus, a 16px gap, then the green-OUTLINED 'Turn on auto-call' key (Reset demo's red confirm stays the only filled lamp key). Escape cancels and focus returns to the switch. Off is immediate and cancels waiting calls; a role=status line reports the result, errors in Lamp Red.
components.html:
Auto-call on
Rings opted-in applicants' phones by itself, 09:00–18:00 UAE, for applications checked from now on. Checks still run before every call.

components.name: Case Auto-Call Line
components.description: Calling Board row between the pre-dial table and the call keys, behind a board-rule top border: lamp + 13px Doto state word (QUEUED/CALLING amber, PLACED green, STOPPED/CANCELLED/OFF unlit at 50%) + a 13px sentence at 75% LED text, sr-only 'Automatic call:' prefix, and a small board key for Stop / Resume automatic calls. Cancelled reasons reuse the pre-dial checks' own words joined with ' · '. The only place the board reports the queue.
components.html:

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Service Hall"**

The application is a numbered ticket from a residency service hall, and the hall's black LED board always says where it is and what happens next. Two materials carry everything. The working surface is cool thermal paper printed in near-black ink: the form, the ticket, the issue list. The status surface is a near-black LED board whose dot-matrix lamps light amber while checking, green when done, red when attention is needed, blue when someone else must act. The hall itself is a pale cool grey floor that both materials sit on.

The world is calm and dense. The hall feels like a public counter where things are being dealt with, not like a dashboard. One bilingual sans (Readex Pro, Latin and Arabic) carries everything a person reads. The ticket prints in thermal mono. Dot-matrix appears only where a real board would light it: reference numerals, the "now serving" stage, short state words. Arabic is true RTL. Columns, lamps and ticket rows mirror; reference numbers and passport data stay LTR inside fixed character cells.

The world rejects the generic government blue-header stepper form and its startup-gradient opposite.

The operator console (`/console`) is built in the same world, unchanged: an officer's counter desk. The queue, the pre-dial calling board, the live call board, the latency board and every lit count are LED board; the open case file, correction slips, call records, logs and the case-history roll are thermal paper. Same tokens, same issue ramp, same lamp states, same motion grammar ("paper feeds down, LED cells light; nothing else moves"). The console is English-only and always LTR.

Waiting, failure and absence are the same world too. While a page loads, the form is already pre-printed and the board is already hung: every fixed label prints, only the data is unprinted paper or an unlit board, at its real size. When a page fails, it says so in plain words on paper under the same bar, with one way forward.

The pitch deck (`brag-output/pitch/deck.html`) is the same world presented, unchanged: 1920 x 1080 slides on the hall floor, type at about twice the app's scale, and the product's real elements (the ticket, its boards, issue rows, status headlines) placed on the floor as themselves, with at most one paper slip per slide pointing at the thing that matters.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials only: thermal paper (working) and LED board (status), on a cool hall-grey floor.
The reference number always sits in fixed character cells: reverse-printed ink on paper, glowing amber on the board.
One fixed three-step issue ramp (fixable / route / officer) used identically everywhere.
Each type role has one job: Readex reads, Geist Mono prints, Doto lights.
Motion is mechanical and diegetic: paper feeds, cells drop, lamps light.
Full EN/AR parity with true RTL on the applicant portal; data stays LTR. The officer console is English and LTR.
Loading screens are the pre-printed form: labels print, data is unprinted ink or unlit lamps, nothing jumps when it arrives.

rules.name: The Two Materials Rule
rules.body: Every surface is either paper (ink on cool white) or board (lamps on black). There is no third material: no tinted cards, no gradients, no glass.

rules.name: The Lamps Stay On The Board Rule
rules.body: LED green, red, blue and amber glow only on board black. On paper, issue weight is expressed with the paper-side ramp (fix / route / officer), never with a lamp colour.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Fixable, route and officer map to the same three colours on every surface: lamp, chip, label, row. Do not add a fourth weight. Do not reuse a ramp colour for decoration. A refusal or an event source is not an issue weight: it takes the neutral chip (ink on Quiet Paper), never officer red.

rules.name: The Done Ink Rule
rules.body: On paper, done reads in Stamp Green (ok) ink, as text or on Quiet Paper. On the board, done is Lamp Green. The two never swap materials.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Readex reads, Geist Mono prints, Doto lights. Dot-matrix is limited to reference numerals, lit counts and figures on a board, the current stage, row state words and the hall monogram. Never use it for sentences, labels or headings.

rules.name: The Equal Scripts Rule
rules.body: Arabic is set in the same family, size and weight as English. Doto has no Arabic glyphs, so in RTL the board's state words switch deliberately to Readex semibold 14px in the lamp colour, never a browser fallback; Geist Mono falls back to Readex for Arabic. A lit word reads as a lamp in both scripts.

rules.name: The One Digit System Rule
rules.body: A screen uses one set of digits. The reference prints in Latin digits in its cells, so Arabic screens format times, dates and counts with Latin digits too (ar-AE-u-nu-latn).

rules.name: The Objects Lift Rule
rules.body: Only physical hall objects (ticket and case-history roll, board, machine, sheet) cast shadows. Cards, slips, log tables, inputs and buttons are flat.

rules.name: The Paper Can't Glow Rule
rules.body: Glow belongs to lamps. Reference cells on paper are reverse-printed ink with no glow. The same cells on the board glow amber.

rules.name: The Pre-Printed Form Rule
rules.body: The form is pre-printed; the data isn't printed yet. Anything that is the same for every case prints as real text while waiting; only case data is unprinted paper (ink at 7%) or unlit board (LED text at 8%, lamps at 25%, blank cells). Every block sits at its real size. No shimmer sweep, no grey boxes standing in for labels.

rules.name: The Refusals Light Red Rule
rules.body: A call action lights by what our backend answered, not by whether the request got through. A refusal sent as a normal reply (ok: false, verified: false, locked: true in the tool's full answer), a blocked tool or a transport error lights Lamp Red with Refused, never green Done; only an answer that refuses nothing lights Done. This is Product Principle 5, every refusal is visible, on the board. On paper a refusal still takes the neutral chip (The One Ramp Rule).

rules.name: The Page Never Promises A Call Rule
rules.body: The status page promises a call only when one is queued, and says when in words the queue can keep. Otherwise an officer arranges the call or will contact the applicant. The applicant is never told to wait for a call nothing will place.

rules.name: The Lift The Shape Rule
rules.body: A lifted cut-out casts its shadow from its own alpha shape (filter: drop-shadow), so the ticket's teeth and a board's rounded corners throw their real outline. Never a box-shadow on the image's rectangle. Flat cut-outs (issue rows, a status headline) stay flat, like the cards they are.

dos: Do build every new surface from the two materials: thermal paper (ink on paper) for working content, LED board (lamps on board black) for status, queues and live state.
Do show any reference number in fixed character cells: reverse-printed ink on paper, glowing amber on the board, always LTR.
Do express issue weight only through the fix / route / officer ramp, identically on lamp, chip, label and row.
Do use the amber "checking" hold before any board row settles on its result.
Do light a call action by our backend's answer: Refused in Lamp Red for any refusal, Done in green only when nothing was refused.
Do keep the amber prototype banner at the top of every screen, including `/console`.
Do set Arabic in Readex at the same size and weight as English, mirror the layout, and keep passport and reference data LTR.
Do render the operator console's queue, call checks and counts as LED Board, and its case file, slips, logs and history as paper, with the same tokens, ramp and motion grammar.
Do keep Approve the primary key on a correction slip, and keep Reject at the far end of the row behind a required, typed reason.
Do print every case event (calls, SMS, handoffs, refusals, decisions) on the one case-history roll.
Do use one digit system per screen: Latin digits on Arabic screens, matching the reference cells.
Do let the h1 name where a link or case stands; a notice under it says only what that means and what to do next.

Do build loading screens as the pre-printed form: fixed labels in real text, only case data unprinted (7% ink) or unlit (8% LED text, 25% lamps), every block at its real size, one status sentence for screen readers.
Do keep whatever still works on screen when part of a page fails or loads: the bar, the tabs, the queue board.
Do give every error screen one primary "Try again", an exit where there is one, and the mono error reference.
Do ask first, inline on the board, before switching on anything that acts by itself on real phones; switching it off is immediate.
Do promise the applicant a call only when one is queued; otherwise say an officer will arrange it or contact them.
Do keep the pitch deck's bottom-right 400 x 400 empty and its prototype line on every slide, and lift cut-out product elements by their own shape (drop-shadow), never by their rectangle.
donts: Don't use the generic government blue-header stepper form, or its startup-gradient opposite.
Don't put LED lamp colours (led-green, led-red, led-blue, led-amber) on paper as text or fills. Use the paper-side ramp, and Stamp Green (ok) for done.
Don't mark refusals, sources or other non-issue states with the officer ramp. Use the neutral chip.
Don't set sentences, headings or labels in Doto. Dot-matrix is for numerals, the current stage and short state words.
Don't add glow to anything on paper, or shadows to anything that isn't a hall object (ticket and case-history roll, board, machine, sheet).

Don't animate anything outside the paper-feed, cell-drop and lamp-lighting grammar. No hover lifts or arrow nudges, no press-in, no page transitions, no looping pulses. The live lamp is steady. The one exception is the slow wait breathe on unprinted and unlit waiting shapes.
Don't pre-tick consent, or place a destructive action beside the primary action.
Don't sweep a shimmer across a skeleton, or stand grey boxes in for words that are the same on every case.
Don't show server error text on an error screen; show the plain-language notice and the digest.
Don't give a screen a skeleton when its language is only known from its data (the upload link).
Don't fill a board key with a lamp colour except Reset demo's Lamp Red confirm; other board confirms are outlined in their lamp colour.
Don't show ElevenLabs' internal workflow tools (notify_condition_*, transfer_to_agent) as actions, or make a live transcript a live region; screen readers hear the turning points only.
